messages.author: 9aad2d2757db1449
messages.subject: x axis in plots
parts:
Hi Phil,

Is it possible to change the x axis limits in the plots? the xlim argument doesn't work, and i get my plots truncated between -4 and 4,
even though I have estimates beyond those limits.

I am sure there is a simple way around this, but I couldn't find it!

Thanks!
Carolina

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: x axis in plots
parts:
Hi Carolina,

Yes you can for most plots, and as of the latest release all internal
plots are handled with the high-end lattice package. To modify the
xlim, simply pass the argument to your plotting function and lattice
will take care of the rest. E.g.,

mod <- mirt(Science, 1)
itemplot(mod, 1)
itemplot(mod, 1, xlim = c(-5,5))

The question is whether you really want to do that or not, since
outside this range the internals are not actually evaluated. Perhaps
building your custom plot manually would make sense? There are a good
number of lower level tools available for doing this, like
probtrace(), iteminfo(), expected.item(), etc.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: x axis in plots
parts:
Just an update; there is a new theta_lim input on the dev for adjusting the range of the evaluated theta. Default is theta_lim = c(-4,4), and to accomplish your goal of extending the axes just change theta_lim = c(-5,5), or whatever else. Cheers.

Phil
